intro: The weather forecast, the shapes of the land and how to place somewhere on the map.
p.borrasca.consejo: It is feminine: «una borrasca». The rr is strong: bo-RRAS-ka.
p.anticiclón.consejo: It has an accent because it ends in n with final stress: an-ti-thi-KLÓN. It brings clear skies.
p.chaparrón.consejo: It has an accent on the o. It comes and goes fast: «un chaparrón de verano».
p.trueno.consejo: The verb is «tronar»: «truena». It is heard after the lightning.
p.relámpago.consejo: It has an accent on the a: rre-LÁM-pa-go. You see it before you hear the thunder.
p.helada.consejo: It comes from «helar». You say «caer una helada» or «hay heladas».
p.templado.consejo: It is said of climate, water or weather: «un invierno templado».
p.previsión.consejo: It has an accent: pre-bi-SIÓN. «Previsión del tiempo» or «parte meteorológico».
p.cordillera.consejo: The ll sounds like y: kor-di-YE-ra. The Pyrenees are a mountain range.
p.llanura.consejo: The ll sounds like y: ya-NU-ra. It comes from «llano», flat.
p.meseta.consejo: The centre of Spain is a large plateau. It is higher than a plain.
p.cabo.consejo: It is written with b. «Al cabo de un año» means «after a year».
p.estrecho.consejo: It is also an adjective: «una calle estrecha». The Strait of Gibraltar separates Europe and Africa.
p.limitar con.consejo: You say «limita al norte con Francia». «Limitar» is also to set a limit.
b1.texto:
**The forecast.** It speaks of **borrascas** (low pressure: wind and rain) and **anticiclones** (high pressure: stable weather).

**Rain and storms.** A **chaparrón** is a heavy, short rain. In a storm there are **relámpagos** and **truenos**. Weather verbs have no subject: **llueve**, **nieva**, **graniza**. In the cold, **heladas** fall.

**Temperature.** It can be **templada** (mild), cold or hot. The wind blows.

**Landforms.** A **cordillera** is a chain of mountains; a **llanura**, flat land; a **meseta**, flat high land.

**The coast.** A **cabo** juts into the sea; a gulf and a bay are inlets; an **estrecho** is a passage between two lands.

**Placing.** **Limita al norte con** Francia; **está situado en** el norte; the river **desemboca en** the sea. Population density is inhabitants per square kilometre.
b2.f1.texto: They say a low-pressure system will arrive from the Atlantic.
b2.f2.texto: Will there be downpours in the afternoon?
b2.f3.texto: There will be thunder and lightning in the mountains.
b2.f4.texto: Then we will not cross the mountain range until Sunday.
b2.f5.texto: On Sunday, with the high pressure, the weather will be mild.
b2.f6.texto: Our village borders the plain to the north.
b2.f7.texto: From the cape you can see the strait on clear days.
b4.texto:
**Weather verbs.** They have no subject: **llueve**, **nieva**, **graniza**, **truena**. With **hay** you name what exists: **hay niebla**, **hay heladas**.

**Placing a location.** **Limita con** + place (**limita al norte con** Francia), **está situado en** + place, **desemboca en** + sea.

Cardinal points take **a** (**al norte**, **al oeste**) or **en** (**en el norte**).
b4.e0.texto: Tomorrow it will hail across the whole mountain range.
b4.e1.texto: At night there is frost on the plateau.
b4.e2.texto: The country borders France to the north.
b5.f0.texto: From the train window, the plateau stretches golden to the horizon.
b5.f1.texto: Not a single tree breaks the straight line of the plain.
b5.f2.texto: In the distance, a blue mountain range seems to float above the dry earth.
b5.f3.texto: The air smells of dust and warm thyme.
b5.f4.texto: A dark cloud grows slowly in the west and puts out the colour of the fields.
b5.f5.texto: Soon the wind starts to blow hard between the tracks.
b5.f6.texto: A white flash of lightning tears the sky and lights the whole plain.
b5.f7.texto: Then the downpour beats on the roof of the train like a handful of stones.
b5.f8.texto: The travellers silently watch the water running down the windows.
b5.f9.texto: Half an hour later, the storm moves away to the east and leaves the earth steaming.
b6.o0.refuerzo: That is what a high-pressure system brings.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Yes: the low-pressure system brings wind and rain.
b6.o2.refuerzo: A frost is cold, not the sign of a low-pressure system.
b6.pregunta: What does a low-pressure system usually bring?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «limitar con» is having a common border.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Límite» is a noun; here a verb is needed.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Frontera» is a noun; here a verb is needed.
b7.pregunta: Which verb says two countries touch?
b8.frase: Mañana soplará viento fuerte en la costa
b8.traduccion: Tomorrow a strong wind will blow on the coast
b9.o0.refuerzo: A frost is cold that freezes water.
b9.o1.refuerzo: A gentle wind is not rain.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Yes: it rains hard, but for a short time.
b11.o0.refuerzo: Yes: light arrives before the sound, the thunder.
b11.o1.refuerzo: A «cabo» is a point of land in the sea.
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: a plateau is flat but high up.
b12.o1.refuerzo: A mountain has a peak; a plateau is flat.
b12.o2.refuerzo: A valley is low, between mountains.
p.chaparrones.consejo: Masculine plural: «el chaparrón». The rr is strong.
p.truenos.consejo: Masculine plural: «el trueno». The u is heard in «tru».
p.relámpagos.consejo: Masculine plural: «el relámpago». The accent is on LAM.
p.cruzaremos.consejo: Future of «cruzar». The z sounds like «th» in Spain.
p.limita.consejo: «Limitar con» means to share a border with. Stress on MI.
p.granizará.consejo: Used with no subject, for weather: «granizará».
p.heladas.consejo: The h is silent. Feminine plural: «la helada».
p.flotar.consejo: The stress is on TAR. «Flotar» and «flota» are related.
p.tomillo.consejo: The ll sounds like «y»: to-MI-yo. Masculine.
p.soplar.consejo: «Soplar» can be used for wind too: «sopla el viento».
p.rasga.consejo: The initial r is strong: RRAS-ga.
p.puñado.consejo: The ñ sounds like «ny»: pu-NYA-do. Masculine: «el puñado».
p.soplará.consejo: Third person future. The stress is on RA.
p.terreno.consejo: Masculine: «el terreno». The rr is strong.
